items.title: Jessie Charles Interview, 1967-12-15
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] I remember one job you played clarinet on because we went a special kind of job to send Kid Sheik off.

ctx.x: No, he didn't play that. No, he didn't play that. I was playing tenor when I first started the brass band. I was playing tenor saxophone. I don't know what I was doing. John Kasman, George. And later on when I began to fool around with Dixieland, I mean I got an interest in winning the Dixieland band here late these late years, I picked up my clarinet again. And I played a few jobs on the clarinet with Abby Williams and guys like that. But the more it was my clarinet job I went to tenor.
I remember one job you played clarinet on because we went a special kind of job to send Kid Sheik off. Yeah, yeah, yeah. And they had a brass band at the train station. Yeah, yeah, yeah.

It's a different kind of job. That's right. That's more of a donation. Like when they play, you know, send guys off or go meet guys like that. But I know that's more of a donation. If you want to go, you know, just donate your service like that. It's okay. Just like a lot of funerals we play. A lot of funerals we play for different members, you know, union guys. It's okay. It's just if you want to donate your service. Yeah, it's okay. Yeah. And we donate our service to George Williams and John Casmick. And it…
